confidence_notes: Food anchors are based on aggregated cost-of-living figures from searches for Naha and Okinawa: CityCost, Mylifeelsewhere, Expatistan, Worksploring, Expatica citing Numbeo data for Okinawa as of June 2026, and combien-coute.net. Typical figures were about JPY 830-1,000 for an inexpensive meal, JPY 4,000-6,300 for a mid-range meal for two and JPY 430-650 for a cappuccino. Some aggregators list draft beer at only JPY 270-325, which looks more like a supermarket or happy-hour price than a standard restaurant serving. For that reason the beer anchor is set higher, reflecting about JPY 500-600 for a draft Orion at a typical Naha izakaya. I found no aggregated cocktail or wine prices. The cocktail anchor is based on its usual relationship to beer in Japanese izakaya and bars, at about 1.5-1.8x beer, or about JPY 800-1,000. The wine anchor is based on izakaya house wine at about JPY 600-800, since the only Naha wine-bar listings found (2024 blog, JPY 1,200-1,600) seem to be specialty pours. USD conversion assumes about JPY 152-160 per USD, which is not verified for July 2026 and adds uncertainty. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge model estimates for July high season in Naha, with no booking searches. Peak summer demand and typhoon-season swings make them the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Japanese regional cities with large tourist numbers, such as Fukuoka and Kagoshima, as comparables. Restaurant prices were set slightly above the Japanese regional average, in line with sources saying Naha restaurants are a few percent above the national level. Accommodation was raised for Okinawa's July beach high season.
